original_question: Determine the least Frobenius variety that contains all complete intersection numerical semigroups.
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Presentations of a numerical semigroup), unnumbered open problem: "What is the least Frobenius variety containing all the complete intersection numerical semigroups?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact unnumbered open problem in Section 5, essentially differing only by replacing the paper’s interrogative phrasing with an imperative one. It also keeps the scope correctly restricted to complete intersection numerical semigroups, without drifting to the larger class of symmetric semigroups or to the neighboring quotient question.
missing_details: The ambient objects should be specified: numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℕ, where ℕ = {0,1,2,...}.

To make the question stand-alone, 'Frobenius variety' should be defined as a nonempty family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T ∈ 𝒱 implies S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱, and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S.
The phrase 'least Frobenius variety' should be made explicit as least with respect to inclusion among Frobenius varieties.

Equivalently, the question can specify that one wants the Frobenius variety generated by the family of all complete intersection numerical semigroups, namely the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing that family.

If 'complete intersection numerical semigroup' is not left as standard terminology, it should be identified with the paper’s nearby definition: a numerical semigroup whose minimal presentation has cardinality e(S) - 1, where e(S) is the embedding dimension of S.
No extra hypotheses should be added: the paper does not fix embedding dimension, genus, Frobenius number, symmetry type, or quotient parameter for this question.
refined_question: Let CI be the family of all complete intersection numerical semigroups, i.e. numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℕ whose minimal presentations have cardinality e(S) - 1, where e(S) denotes the embedding dimension of S. Determine the Frobenius variety generated by CI, that is, the smallest family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups containing CI such that: (i) if S,T ∈ 𝒱, then S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱; and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S.
equivalent_formulation: Determine the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing the family of all complete intersection numerical semigroups.
justification: The draft matches the exact second open question posed in Section 5 immediately after the paper defines complete intersections via minimal presentations. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import from Section 4 the definitions of Frobenius variety and of the Frobenius variety generated by a family. The gluing discussion that follows in Section 5 is relevant nearby context because it gives Delorme’s structural characterization of complete intersections, but the paper does not replace the Frobenius-variety question by a broader gluing-closure problem; so the refined version should stay exactly at the level of determining the generated Frobenius variety of the class of complete intersection numerical semigroups.
